% scaling_overall_permodel.pdf; expG4/G5's rejection of full parallelism).
% Generated by hand (no new computation) alongside table_scaling_modelselection.py;
% see the footnotes below for the specific finding backing each checkmark.
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
$F_i$ family & Diminishing & Category & Firm & Persistent comp. & Cross-category \\
             & returns     & heterog. & heterog. & advantage$^\dagger$    & spillovers$^\ddagger$ \\
\midrule
$a_i\log(1+x)\mathbf{1}$                & \checkmark & $\times$   & \checkmark & $\times$   & $\times$ \\

% Evidence backing each column:
%
% Diminishing returns -- built into log(1+x) for rows 1-3 by construction, but
%   also empirically supported, not just assumed: Table 3's fitted power-law
%   exponent gamma-hat = 0.13 (mean over 5 folds), sharply sub-linear, and a
%   raw-linear F loses to log/power-law forms on held-out error.
%
% Category heterogeneity -- rejected by row 1 (a scalar a_i cannot vary by k).
%   Needs row >= 2. Evidence: scaling_by_category.pdf shows real slope spread
%   across categories (BBH +1.14 vs IFEval +0.75, pooled across labs); Table 3
%   shows going from firm-only to firm x category parameters buys a further
%   +31.8% held-out error reduction, dwarfing the +0.8% firm-only gets alone --
%   i.e. nearly all of the real heterogeneity in this data is CATEGORY-specific,
%   not firm-specific in a category-blind sense.
%
% Firm heterogeneity -- present from row 1 on (a_i differs by firm). Evidence:
%   scaling_overall_permodel.pdf (Arcee AI +1.90 vs EleutherAI +0.01); G4's
%   ||A_i|| spans 0.43-2.19 (~5x).
%
% $\dagger$ Persistent comparative advantage -- row 1 is DIRECTLY falsified by
%   the persistence HAC tests, not just under-flexible: Anthropic is
%   significantly POSITIVE on Coding (mean +11.9, t=+3.94, p=0.00008) and
%   significantly NEGATIVE on English (mean -20.6, t=-20.18) at the same time --
%   a single scalar a_i cannot produce opposite-signed, category-specific,
%   persistent deviations for the same firm. Needs row >= 2.
%
% $\ddagger$ Cross-category spillovers -- the one property in this table we have
%   NOT directly tested. Rows 3-4 are the only families that CAN represent it
%   (off-diagonal A_i terms / a fully flexible F), but nothing here isolates a
%   genuine spillover from mere per-category heterogeneity (row 2 already
%   explains the persistence and category-heterogeneity findings on its own).
%   Experiment D's category-launch natural experiment is the closest attempt at
%   a direct test and came back "suggestive, not established" (one effective
%   episode, not several -- see the natural-experiment discussion). Treat the
%   checkmarks in this column as "the family COULD generate this," not as
%   confirmed necessity.
